evals.prompt: Our descaling guide gets plenty of impressions but almost no clicks — that's from our own Search Console screenshots; no tools are connected here. The current tags and the visible page copy are in evals/files/blog-descale-espresso-en.md. Target keyword: 'how to descale an espresso machine'. Fix the title and meta description, and give us A/B variants to try.
evals.expected_output: A before/after optimization: the 128-character brand-first title and the missing description are diagnosed with character counts; the recommended title is 60 characters or fewer with 'descale … espresso machine' front-loaded and Beanhaus demoted to the end; the recommended description is 130-160 characters with the keyword and a CTA. Every proposed tag and A/B variant stays inside the fixture's facts (five steps, about 25 minutes, 2 tablespoons per litre, every three months, £4.50 for 250g, the 2026 date) — no invented step counts, ratings, 'free' extras, or awards, and no placeholder text inside any tag string.
expectations: The current-tag diagnosis flags both fixture defects: the existing title is reported as over the skill's limit — SKILL.md requires 'Length: 50-60 characters (displays fully in SERP)' and the formulas reference lists 'Exceeding 60 characters' as a mistake ('Key info truncated in SERP') — with a stated character count between 118 and 138 (the fixture title is 128 characters), and the page's missing meta description is called out.

The recommended title is 30-60 characters — the pass band is the union of the skill's own display rows ('30-50 characters: Fully displayed on all devices', '50-60 characters: Full display on desktop'; under 30 'May appear thin', over 60 truncates) — and every proposed title option and A/B variant carries a stated character count that matches the true length of its string within ±2 characters (the skill's Character Counting function must be real, not decorative).

Keyword placement follows the skill's rules in the recommended title: 'descale' and 'espresso machine' appear together as one phrase (e.g. 'Descale an Espresso Machine', with or without the 'how to' prefix) starting in the first half of the title — per SKILL.md 'Include primary keyword (preferably near front)' and the /seo:optimize-meta scaffold tip 'Front-load primary keyword in the first half of the title tag' — and the brand, if kept, moves to the end after a separator per the formulas-reference fix for 'Brand name first (non-branded query)': 'Put brand at end after pipe'; a recommended title that again opens with 'Beanhaus' fails.

A meta description is delivered at 130-160 characters — at most 160 per the skill's display rule ('Length: 150-160 characters (displays fully in SERP)'), at least 130 (the floor of the skill's own description templates, which run ~130-160) — containing the primary keyword naturally and a clear call-to-action per the requirements 'Include primary keyword naturally' and 'Include clear call-to-action', with its stated character count accurate within ±2.

No fabrication in any proposed tag — title, description, OG/Twitter value, or A/B test variant. Supported concretes from the fixture: five steps, about 25 minutes, 2 tablespoons per 1 litre, every three months, £4.50 for a 250g tub (about six descales), the February 2026 date, Beanhaus, home/pump espresso machines. Anything else fails: a different step count ('7 Steps'), any rating or review count, 'Free' anything (the skill's own worked example models a '(+ Free Checklist)' variant — no checklist or free item exists on this page), awards, reader counts, or invented product claims (ledger F3 guard).

Zero placeholder or provenance text inside any proposed tag string (ledger F13 placement lesson applied to this skill's paste-ready surface): no bracketed tokens ('[Brand]', '[Number]', '[Year]'), no 'TBD'/'XX', and no data-needed markers appear inside a proposed <title>, meta description, or social tag value — a tag that would need unavailable data is flagged in the report prose and ships complete without the unavailable claim.

evals.prompt: All three of our city pages share one title and one meta description — current tags and each page's copy are in evals/files/city-pages-duplicate-titles-en.md. Google keeps showing the Leeds page for York cleaning searches. Keywords per page: 'domestic cleaning leeds', 'end of tenancy cleaning york', 'cleaners harrogate'. Give every page its own title and description we can paste straight in.
evals.expected_output: A per-page tag set: the duplicate title/description problem is named with the skill's cannibalization consequence and unique-per-page fix; Leeds, York, and Harrogate each get a unique title of at most 60 characters (city + service keyword front-loaded) and a unique 130-160-character description with a CTA, differentiated by each page's own facts. Harrogate — whose copy supports no strong claim — ships modest, accurate tags, with its missing proof elements flagged in the report rather than compensated by invention; no ratings, '24/7', customer counts, or placeholder tokens appear anywhere in the set.
expectations: The audit names the duplication with the skill's own consequence and fix: duplicate titles across the three pages per the formulas-reference mistakes row 'Duplicate titles across pages' — 'Cannibalization; Google may pick wrong page' — 'Unique title per page' (which also explains the user's Leeds-shown-for-York symptom), and the shared meta description is flagged against the requirement 'Avoid duplicate descriptions'.

Three unique titles are delivered, pairwise different, one per page: each is 30-60 characters (the skill's display band; over 60 truncates), each contains its own city name (Leeds / York / Harrogate) and its page's service keyword ('domestic cleaning' / 'end of tenancy cleaning' / 'cleaners' or 'cleaning'), with the service+city material starting in the first half per 'Include primary keyword (preferably near front)'; the brand, if included, sits at the end after a separator.

Three unique meta descriptions are delivered, pairwise different, each 130-160 characters, each including its page's keyword naturally and a clear call-to-action — per 'Include primary keyword naturally', 'Include clear call-to-action', and 'Avoid duplicate descriptions'.

Differentiation is content-true, not invented: York's tags draw on that page's actual copy (end of tenancy specialism, from £145 for a one-bedroom flat, or the 48-hour re-clean), Leeds's on its own (since 2012, insured and DBS-checked, from £16 per hour, 14 cleaners, or the free no-obligation quote) — and page-specific numbers never migrate: £16/hour or '14 cleaners' outside the Leeds tags, or £145 / the 48-hour re-clean outside the York tags, fails.

Harrogate is handled as the honesty case: its page copy supports only 'cleaning services for homes in the Harrogate area' by BrightNest, so its tags stay modest — service + area + brand, optionally plus facts the fixture states company-wide ('BrightNest has cleaned homes across Yorkshire since 2012', 'Every cleaner is insured and DBS-checked', 'every job starts with a free, no-obligation quote') — and carry NO Harrogate-specific price, team size, specialism, guarantee, or proof element (none exists in its copy); the report flags the Harrogate page's missing proof/specifics as data to collect or content to add (the skill's CTR-elements analysis), never compensating inside the tag.

No fabrication anywhere in the set and no placeholder text inside any tag (ledger F3 + F13 guards): nothing appears that no fixture page supports — no star ratings, review counts, '24/7', awards, '#1', customer totals, or invented offers — and no bracketed or provenance tokens ('[City]', '[Price]', 'TBD', data-needed markers) ship inside any proposed title or description; missing-data notes belong in the report prose.

evals.prompt: Η σελίδα κατηγορίας με τα σανδάλια μας κληρονόμησε το title της αρχικής και δεν έχει καθόλου meta description — τα τρέχοντα tags και το κείμενο της σελίδας είναι στο evals/files/eshop-sandalia-category-el.md. Λέξη-κλειδί: «χειροποίητα σανδάλια». Γράψε νέο title tag και νέα meta description στα ελληνικά, με μέτρημα χαρακτήρων, για να τα περάσουμε όπως είναι στη σελίδα.
evals.expected_output: Native-Greek replacement tags with accurate character counts: the ≈123-character homepage-style title and the missing description are flagged; the new Greek title (at most 60 characters, counted on the Greek string) front-loads «Χειροποίητα Σανδάλια», and the new Greek description (130-160 characters) uses only the page's facts (Χανιά, από το 1987, 45 σχέδια, νούμερα 35-46, από 39 €, παράδοση 1-3 εργάσιμες, μεταφορικά 3,50 €) with a Greek CTA — fluent, correctly accented Greek throughout, no «δωρεάν μεταφορικά», no ratings, and no placeholder text inside the tags.
expectations: The current-tag audit flags the fixture title as over-limit and homepage-generic: a stated character count between 113 and 133 (the fixture title is 123 characters) against SKILL.md's 'Length: 50-60 characters (displays fully in SERP)', its «Αρχική Σελίδα» opening tied to the generic-title mistake ('Too generic ("Home", "Welcome")' — 'Zero CTR differentiation'), and the missing meta description called out.

The proposed title is native Greek, 30-60 characters counted on the Greek string itself (the multi-language reference's principle 'Character limits vary' — counting the actual characters, not words), with «χειροποίητα σανδάλια» in a natural case/inflection (e.g. «Χειροποίητα Σανδάλια») starting in the first half per 'Include primary keyword (preferably near front)'; its stated character count is accurate within ±2.

The proposed meta description is native Greek, 130-160 characters (at most 160 per 'Length: 150-160 characters'; at least 130, the floor of the skill's own templates) with a stated count accurate within ±2, includes the keyword naturally, and contains a clear Greek call-to-action (e.g. «Δείτε τη συλλογή», «Παραγγείλετε online») per 'Include clear call-to-action'.

Greek output quality (watch-item W4 guard, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md): both proposed tags read as fluent, idiomatic Greek a native reader would accept on a Greek e-shop — correct diacritics (tonos) throughout, correct final sigma (ς), natural retail phrasing, no translation-ese, no Greeklish, and no untranslated English boilerplate (e.g. 'Shop now', 'Home') inside the Greek tag strings.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every concrete in the proposed tags traces to the fixture. Supported: Χανιά (και Κρήτη), από το 1987, 45 σχέδια, ανδρικά και γυναικεία, νούμερα 35-46, από 39 €, δέρμα φυτικής δέψης, χειροποίητη κατασκευή στο εργαστήριο, παράδοση σε όλη την Ελλάδα σε 1-3 εργάσιμες, μεταφορικά 3,50 €, αλλαγή/επιστροφή εντός 14 ημερών. Fails: «δωρεάν μεταφορικά»/«δωρεάν αποστολή» (shipping costs 3,50 €), any rating («4,9/5», αστέρια), review or customer count, «Νο1», award, discount/«προσφορά»/«έκπτωση», or a changed count ('50+ σχέδια').

Zero placeholder or provenance text inside the proposed Greek tags (ledger F13 placement lesson): no «[ΜΑΡΚΑ]»-style or '[Brand]'-style tokens, no data-needed markers like «απαιτούνται στοιχεία», no 'TBD' — the tags ship paste-ready («όπως είναι», as the user asked); anything the page's data cannot support is flagged in the report prose and simply omitted from the tag.

evals.prompt: We launch the German version of our villa site next week. The head snippets from all three language pages plus the sitemap excerpt are in evals/files/hreflang-villa-set-el-en-de.md. Run the six-point hreflang checklist over the set and give us the corrected blocks for each page.
evals.expected_output: A six-point checklist audit naming all seeded defects — the EN block missing the el return link, the DE block missing its own de self-entry, the cluster's conflicting x-default targets, the EL canonical pointing at the EN page, hreflang="gr" instead of "el", and the sitemap missing /el/villa/ — followed by corrected markup per the skill's EL/EN/DE example: an identical el/en/de alternate set with self-references on all three pages, self-referential canonicals, exactly one consistent x-default (the EN page), hreflang="el", and 1:1 sitemap alignment. Only the three fixture URLs appear.
expectations: Defect set A (tag-block structure) is identified against the skill's Hreflang Checklist: (i) the EN page's block omits the el alternate — row a, 'Every variant's tag block lists ALL variants, including itself (bidirectional)', fails when 'Page A → B exists but B → A is missing'; (ii) the DE page's block omits its own de self-entry — the same row's including-itself clause; (iii) the cluster declares two different x-default targets (EL and EN blocks point x-default at the EN page, the DE block at the DE page) — row b, 'Exactly one hreflang="x-default" per cluster'.

Defect set B (canonical, language code, sitemap) is identified: (iv) the Greek page's canonical points at the EN page — row c, 'Each variant's <link rel="canonical"> points to itself — never to another language version' (the checklist's own fails-when: 'EL/DE canonical points to the EN "master" page'); (v) hreflang="gr" on the Greek alternate — row d, 'Never a bare region/country code as the language', fails when 'hreflang="gr" used instead of el'; (vi) the sitemap mismatch — row e, 'hreflang set matches sitemap <xhtml:link> entries 1:1' (no /el/villa/ entry exists and the listed entries carry only en+de).

Corrected markup is produced for all three pages following the skill's EL/EN/DE example ('identical block on all three pages (canonical self-referential, href swapped per page)') — either three explicit blocks or one block explicitly stated to be identical on all three pages with only the canonical swapped: the alternate set is identical and complete, with el, en, and de entries all present in every block so that every page carries a self-referencing entry.

Each corrected canonical is self-referential: the EL page's canonical is https://www.villa-thalassia.gr/el/villa/, the EN page's is https://www.villa-thalassia.gr/en/villa/, and the DE page's is https://www.villa-thalassia.gr/de/villa/ — none points at another language version.

Exactly one x-default entry exists per corrected block and its target is the same URL across all three pages — the EN page, per the fixture's statement that international visitors default to the English page (matching the skill example's x-default choice) — and every Greek entry uses hreflang="el" (or the language-region form "el-GR" per row d); hreflang="gr" appears nowhere in the corrected markup.

Sitemap alignment is addressed per row e: the response instructs or shows the sitemap carrying all three <loc> URLs — including the currently missing /el/villa/ — with <xhtml:link> alternate entries matching the corrected head blocks 1:1.

No fabrication and no placeholders (ledger F3 + F13 guards): the corrected markup uses only the three fixture URLs on www.villa-thalassia.gr — no invented language versions, subdomains, ccTLD domains, or extra pages — and, since every needed URL is known from the fixture, no '[URL]'-style placeholder appears inside any corrected tag line.

evals.prompt: Write the title tag and meta description for our new pricing page at https://apexmetrics.io/pricing. Target keyword: 'product analytics pricing'. I haven't sent you the page — it's still in the CMS — and no tools are connected here, but we ship tonight, so just write them now.
evals.expected_output: The skill declines to write blind tags: it requests the page's actual content and value proposition (and the real plan facts, if prices are to appear in the tags) per its manual-data mode, explains via the C01 alignment check and the 'Match page content accurately' requirement why tags written without the page would be unverifiable or misleading, and ships nothing presented as paste-ready for the unseen pricing page — no invented plan names, prices, trials, discounts, or 'free' claims, and no pretended read of the URL.
expectations: Instead of shipping blind tags, the response asks for the missing inputs per the skill's manual-data mode ('Ask the user to provide: 1. Current title and meta description (if optimizing existing) 2. Target primary keyword and 2-3 secondary keywords 3. Page URL and main content/value proposition 4. Competitor URLs or examples...'): at minimum it requests the page's actual content / value proposition — for a pricing page, the real plan names and prices if they are to appear in the tags — and it holds this line despite the 'we ship tonight' pressure.

No paste-ready tags for the unseen page: the response contains no <title> or meta description presented as final, recommended, or ready to implement for apexmetrics.io/pricing. The skill's generic formulas (e.g. '[Product] Pricing: [Value Statement]') may be shown only when explicitly framed as templates awaiting the requested content; a clearly-labeled provisional sketch built ONLY from the user-supplied keyword and the brand name in the domain, with no other claims, does not by itself fail — provided shipping is still conditioned on receiving the page content. Any tag carrying concrete claims about ApexMetrics beyond those two supplied strings fails.

No fabrication and no fake tool reads (ledger F3 guard): the response invents no plan names, prices, discounts, trial lengths, feature counts, customer counts, ratings, or 'free' claims for ApexMetrics — zero page facts were supplied, so any such concrete anywhere in the response is fabricated — and it does not claim to have fetched or read the URL (no tools are connected; a 'your page says…'-style attribution fails).

The hold is grounded in the skill's own accuracy rules, not silent: the response explains that tags must match real page content — the C01 alignment check ('Title promise matches actual content delivery'; 'If C01 fails: Title is misleading — rewrite to match actual content') and/or the description requirement 'Match page content accurately' — so the user learns why blind tags are declined; a bare refusal with no reason, or a stall that never states what unblocks it, fails.
